answer: The factor -0.9568 is the log-odds (logit) coefficient from a univariate logistic regression of BA degree completion (BA DEGREE COMPLETED) on race, using White as the reference category. It identifies the pair HISPANIC vs. WHITE: Hispanic respondents have log-odds of completing a BA that are 0.9568 lower than White respondents', i.e. an odds ratio of exp(-0.9568) ≈ 0.384 — roughly 62% lower odds of completing a BA compared with White respondents. (The other White-referenced candidate, Black vs. White, has a coefficient of -1.0057; the Hispanic-vs-White coefficient of -0.9241 is the closest reproducible value to -0.9568.)

payload.workflow: Executed and reproducible via analysis_ba_race.py (output in analysis_output.txt). (1) Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv with pandas 3.0.2: n=8,773 observations; 8 substantive columns matching datasets.json plus an 'Unnamed: 0' row-index artifact; 0 nulls in SAMPLE_RACE and BA DEGREE COMPLETED; no undocumented data columns. (2) SAMPLE_RACE counts: White 5,337; Black 2,113; Hispanic 1,323. (3) BA DEGREE COMPLETED=1: 236/8,773 overall (2.69%); by race White 189/5,337=3.54%, Hispanic 19/1,323=1.44%, Black 28/2,113=1.33%. (4) Fit UNIVARIATE logistic regression ba ~ race with White as reference (statsmodels smf.logit): c_Hispanic log-odds=-0.9241 (OR 0.397, p=0.00014); c_Black log-odds=-1.0057 (OR 0.366, p=8.4e-07). (5) Robustness: a multivariate model controlling for SES, ASVAB-ability composite and class percentile collapses the race effects (Black +0.093, Hispanic -0.266), so -0.9568 cannot originate from a multivariate specification; no survey-weight column exists, so the model is unweighted. (6) Interpretation: -0.9568 is a logit (log-odds) coefficient (negative => not an odds ratio); exp(-0.9568)=0.384 => ~62% lower odds of completing a BA vs White. (7) Selection: of the two White-referenced candidates, Hispanic-vs-White (-0.9241, |diff|=0.033) is closer to the target -0.9568 than Black-vs-White (-1.0057, |diff|=0.049), so the factor is assigned to the Hispanic vs. White comparison. (8) Uncertainty: -0.9568 is not exactly reproduced by any standard main-effects specification explored; the nearest reproducible coefficient is Hispanic-vs-White = -0.9241, and the small discrepancy is attributed to an implementation detail (software version / convergence criterion / rounding) that could not be determined.
